# Why Accounting on Pre-War Tsarist Boundaries Illuminates the 1914-1926AD Catastrophe

Reconstructing the demographic history of the Russian Civil War (1917-1926AD, anchored to a 1914AD pre-war baseline) on the fixed territorial denominator of the forty-eight pre-war Tsarist Governorates and Oblasts (18 607 231 km2 across 460 079 5-arcminute grid cells, including former Congress Poland, the three Baltic Baltic Governorates, the Grand Duchy of Finland, Lithuania, Bessarabia and the adjacent Carpatho-Galician borderlands of Eastern Galicia, Bukovina and Subcarpathian Rus, while excluding Central Asia and the Southern Caucasus) resolves the central accounting problem of early twentieth-century Eurasian demography [@volkov1930dinamika; @lorimer1946population; @holquist2002making; @smele2015russian]. Because the Russian Empire disintegrated between 1917AD and 1921AD into the Soviet republics and seven Central and Eastern European successor states, conventional demographic series bounded by post-1921AD Soviet borders conflate biological excess mortality with border changes, two-way wartime refugee streams and post-treaty repatriations [@gatrell1999whole; @baron2004homelands; @polyakov1986sovetskaya; @andreev1993naselenie]. Holding the forty-eight pre-war administrative units constant exposes the unbroken 1914-1922AD continuum of crisis - First World War mobilisation, the 1915AD Great Retreat (*biezenstwo*), the 1918AD Brest-Litovsk rupture and national wars of independence, multi-front Red-White-Green warfare, urban de-population under War Communism, pandemic typhus and Spanish influenza, and the 1921-1922AD Povolzhye-Ural-Southern Ukrainian famine - before demonstrating at the 1926AD splice exactly how diplomatic treaties detached 37 840k inhabitants into interwar European states and transferred 4 940k across internal Kazakh, Tuvan and western district adjustments, leaving 125 000k inside the 17 December 1926AD All-Union Census core of the RSFSR, Ukrainian SSR and Belorussian SSR [@tsu1926vsesoyuznaya].

Across the entire forty-eight-region footprint, total population contracted from 167 945k (167,95M) in 1914AD to 165 375k (165,38M) at the revolutionary benchmark of 1917AD, fell steadily across the Civil War years (160 600k in 1918AD, 155 965k in 1919AD, 152 045k in 1920AD and 149 545k in 1921AD) to a famine trough of 148 655k (148,66M) in 1922AD - a net loss of 19 290k (-11,5% below 1914AD, or -16 720k and -10,1% below 1917AD, alongside roughly 12M-14M unborn children) - before rebounding under the New Economic Policy (*NEP*) and interwar agrarian reconstruction to 157 800k in 1924AD and 167 780k (167,78M) by December 1926AD [@volkov1930dinamika; @zhiromskaya2000naselenie; @maksudov1989poteri; @pocheshkhov2020poteri] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_pocheshkhov_nurbiy_aslanovich_2020_poteri_naseleniya_v_gody_grazhdanskoy_voyn.pdf)). Excluding the two Habsburg Carpatho-Galician regions (Regions 14-15) and Finland (Regions 8-9), the forty-four Tsarist imperial provinces proper declined from 155 405k (1914AD) and 152 785k (1917AD) to 135 850k (1922AD) before recovering to 153 685k (1926AD).

Eight independent bodies of primary census and statistical documentation anchor our forty-eight-region series without recourse to global macro-historical compendia:

The 1914AD TsSK Statistical Yearbooks and 1917AD All-Russian Agricultural and Municipal Censuses, recording pre-war governorate populations and the 1917AD wartime redistribution of 6,0M-7,0M western refugees (*bezhentsy*) and garrisoned soldiers into central Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian cities [@vseros1917gorod; @vseros1917sel; @gatrell1999whole; @arakelyan2023perepisi] ([archived PDF](papers/soviet_post_stalin_arakelyan_araksya_vanikovna_2023_demograficheskie_perepisi_kak_istochnik_o_.pdf)). The 28 August 1920AD All-Russian Demographic-Occupational Census, conducted by Pavel Popov's Central Statistical Administration (*TsSU RSFSR*) across accessible European and Siberian provinces at the nadir of War Communism urban depopulation [@tsu1920perepis; @koenker1985urbanization].

Finnish Official Vital and Census Statistics (SVT VI, 1917-1926AD) and the War Victims in Finland (1914-1922AD) Registry, providing parish-level population counts across Finland's eight governorates (Regions 8-9), the December 1920AD national census (3 364,8k *de jure*; 3 105,1k present) and individual-level mortality records for the 1918AD Finnish Civil War [@svt1923finland; @rantala2020warvictims; @myrskyla2023finnish] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_myrskyla_santavirta_2023_finnish_civil_war_1918_mortality.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_rantala_jokipii_2020_war_victims_finland_1914_1922.pdf)).

Baltic Independence Censuses (Latvia 1920AD & 1925AD; Estonia 1922AD; Lithuania 1923AD), measuring wartime evacuation losses and post-treaty optation returns across Estland, Livland, Courland, Latgale and Kovno (Regions 5-7, 10, 13) [@estonia1924rahvaloendus; @skujenieks1927latvia; @lithuania1926gyventojai; @gusachenko2021latvia; @marcinkevicius2026lithuania] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_gusacenko_kleinberga_2021_latvia_state_1918.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_marcinkevicius_2026_russians_in_lithuania_1918_1940.pdf)).

The 30 September 1921AD First General Census of the Republic of Poland (GUS), enumerating Congress Poland (Regions 1-4), the Riga *Kresy Wschodnie* across Vilna, Grodno, western Minsk and western Volhynia (Regions 11-12, 17) and Eastern Galicia (Region 14), supplemented by the 1919AD Civil Administration of the Eastern Lands (*ZCZW*) count [@gus1921skorowidz; @barwinski2015ethnic; @cichoracki2014polesia] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_barwinski_2015_polish_census_1921_eastern_borderlands.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_cichoracki_2014_polesia_after_riga_1921.pdf)).

Czechoslovak (15 February 1921AD) and Romanian (1919-1926AD) Enumerations, anchoring Subcarpathian Rus (6k in 1921AD), Bukovina (Region 15) and Bessarabia (Region 16) [@csr1924scitani; @tartakovsky2009bessarabia; @fondos2024bessarabia] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_tartakovsky_2009_bessarabia_jewish_crisis_1918_1926.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_fondos_2024_bessarabia_interwar_population.pdf)). The 15 March 1923AD All-Union Urban Census, capturing early NEP municipal recovery across 1 925 Soviet cities and urban settlements immediately after the 1921-1922AD famine [@tsu1923gorod; @repinetskiy2009nepmany] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_repinetskiy_a_i_2009_nepmany_quot_novye_russkie_quot_1920_kh_gg.pdf)).

The 17 December 1926AD First All-Union Population Census and 1926-1927AD Polar Census, published in 56 volumes under Vasily Mikhailovsky and Osip Kvitkin, providing exact rural and urban counts across all Soviet republics, ASSRs, AOs and northern indigenous territories [@tsu1926vsesoyuznaya; @lorimer1946population].


# Forty-Eight-Region Population Trajectory (1914AD - 1926AD) and the 1926AD Splice

Table \ref{tab:regional-trajectories} reports the complete benchmark population series (1914AD - 1926AD, in thousands) for all forty-eight pre-war Tsarist Governorates and Oblasts across the former empire, grouped into three macro-zones: the Western Imperial and Carpatho-Galician Borderlands (Regions 1-16, 1 022 140 km2), Ukraine and Novorossiya (Regions 17-24, 541 852 km2) and European Russia, the North Caucasus, the Urals, Siberia and the Far East (Regions 25-48, 17 043 239 km2). Figure \ref{fig:fig2-trajectory} plots the divergence in timing and amplitude across eight regional theatres alongside stacked macro-regional volumes.

```{r table-regional-trajectories, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
sum_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON((if (file.exists("russian_civil_war_summary.json")) "russian_civil_war_summary.json" else "../../_shared/_gis_cache/russian_civil_war_summary.json"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
regs <- sum_json$regions
yrs <- c("1914", "1917", "1918", "1919", "1920", "1921", "1922", "1924", "1926")

fmt_k <- function (v) {
  paste0(format(as.integer(round(as.numeric(v))), big.mark = " ", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE), "k")
}

make_reg_row <- function (r) {
  short_nm <- trimws(strsplit(strsplit(as.character(r$name), "\\(")[[1]][1], ":")[[1]][1])
  vals <- lapply(yrs, function (y) fmt_k(r$population_k[[y]]))
  names(vals) <- yrs
  as.data.frame(c(list(`Tsarist Governorate / Oblast` = short_nm), vals), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

make_sub_row <- function (lbl, idx_vec) {
  vals <- lapply(yrs, function (y) {
    s <- sum(vapply(idx_vec, function (i) as.numeric(regs[[i]]$population_k[[y]]), numeric(1)))
    fmt_k(s)
  })
  names(vals) <- yrs
  as.data.frame(c(list(`Tsarist Governorate / Oblast` = lbl), vals), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

rows_1_16 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(regs[1:16], make_reg_row))
sub_1_16 <- make_sub_row("Subtotal Regs 1-16: Western Borderlands", 1:16)
rows_17_24 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(regs[17:24], make_reg_row))
sub_17_24 <- make_sub_row("Subtotal Regs 17-24: Ukraine & Novorossiya", 17:24)
rows_25_48 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(regs[25:48], make_reg_row))
sub_25_48 <- make_sub_row("Subtotal Regs 25-48: Russia, Caucasus & Siberia", 25:48)
tot_all <- make_sub_row("Grand Total (All 48 Tsarist Regions)", 1:48)

full_48_df <- rbind(rows_1_16, sub_1_16, rows_17_24, sub_17_24, rows_25_48, sub_25_48, tot_all)

render_table_template(
  full_48_df,
  list(
    caption = "Regional Population Trajectories Across All Forty-Eight Pre-War Tsarist Governorates and Oblasts (1914AD - 1926AD, in thousands).",
    label = "tab:regional-trajectories",
    col_fracs = c(0.258, rep(0.068, 9))
  )
)
```

```{r fig2-trajectory, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_figure_template(
  "figures/russian_civil_war_fig2_population_trajectory.png",
  list(
    caption = "Indexed regional population trajectories (1914AD = 100, Panel A) and stacked macro-regional totals in millions across the Civil War (1914AD - 1926AD, Panel B).",
    label = "fig:fig2-trajectory",
    span_columns = TRUE
  )
)
```

Holding pre-war boundaries fixed reveals a two-phase spatial inversion between the western borderlands and the Russian interior:

Phase I (1914-1917AD, Mobilisation and the Great Retreat): Regions 1-16 lost 5 125k inhabitants (41 910k to 36 785k, -12,2%) as Tsarist armies forcibly evacuated or triggered flight from Courland, Kovno, Grodno, Vilna, Congress Poland and Volhynia, while Austro-Russian combat displaced hundreds of thousands in Eastern Galicia [@gatrell1999whole; @balkelis2018war]. Conversely, Regions 25-48 gained +2 775k (93 805k to 96 580k, +3,0%) as western refugees, evacuated Baltic and Polish factory workers and rear garrisons crowded into Petrograd, Moscow, the Central Industrial Ring, the Middle and Lower Volga and the Trans-Siberian corridor.

Phase II (1917-1922AD, Civil War, Urban Hollowing, Epidemics and Famine): Once interior Russia and Ukraine plunged into multi-front Civil War and the 1921-1922AD famine, Regions 25-48 suffered a catastrophic net contraction of -14 290k (96 580k down to 82 290k in 1922AD, -14,8%) and Ukraine (Regions 17-24) lost -3 730k (32 010k down to 28 280k, -11,7%), exacerbated by the westward return of Polish, Baltic and Lithuanian evacuees after 1918-1921AD peace treaties (Regions 1-16 bottoming at 36 065k in 1919AD before climbing to 38 085k by 1922AD and 41 428k by 1926AD).

At the December 1926AD terminal splice, Table \ref{tab:splice-1926} and Figure \ref{fig:fig3-subregional}B reconcile the 167 780k population of the forty-eight pre-war Tsarist regions with interwar state boundaries and our subsequent soviet_lenin_stalin epoch (145 070k in 1926AD on post-1945AD USSR borders). Diplomatic treaties between 1917AD and 1921AD placed 37 840k inhabitants (22,6% of the 1926AD total) inside seven sovereign Central and Eastern European states (Second Polish Republic 24 615k, Kingdom of Romania 3 730k, Republic of Finland 3 605k, Republic of Lithuania 2 245k, Republic of Latvia 1 860k, Republic of Estonia 1 115k and Czechoslovakia 670k). Internal Soviet boundary realignments transferred 2 540k steppe inhabitants of Bukey (Astrakhan), southern Orenburg and southern Omsk uezds into the Kazakh ASSR (tracked in the Central Asian regional series), 70k into independent Tannu-Tuva (Uriankhai) and 2 330k across western district adjustments, yielding 125 000k on the exact 1926AD European and Siberian Soviet core (RSFSR + Karelia 92 410k, Ukrainian SSR + Crimea 27 750k and Eastern Belorussian SSR 4 840k). Adding back the 20 070k 1926AD inhabitants of the western territories later annexed by the USSR in 1939-1945AD (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Kaliningrad, Western Belarus, Western Ukraine, Northern Bukovina, Subcarpathia and Moldavia) reproduces the exact 145 070k 1926AD baseline of soviet_lenin_stalin.

# Western Secession, Independence Wars, and Refugee Repatriation

## Former Congress Poland: The Ten Vistula Governorates (Regions 1 - 4)

Across the ten Vistula Governorates of former Congress Poland (116 848 km2; Regions 1-4), pre-war population fell by -2 020k (-14,8%) between 1914AD (13 650k) and 1917AD (11 630k, troughing at 11 520k in 1918AD) under the combined shock of August 1914AD frontier combat (including the German artillery destruction of Kalisz, halving the city from 65,4k to 29,0k), the summer 1915AD Russian Great Retreat (*biezenstwo*) that swept over 1,2M inhabitants eastward, particularly from Lublin, Siedlce, Kholm, Lomza and Suwalki (Region 3 dropping -22,4% from 2 680k to 2 080k), and Central Powers raw-material blockades and labour requisitions [@gatrell1999whole; @barwinski2015ethnic] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_barwinski_2015_polish_census_1921_eastern_borderlands.pdf)). Deprived of Russian cotton markets and British-American raw cotton, textile Lodz (Region 2) contracted from 477,9k (1914AD) to 342,0k (1917AD), while Warsaw (Region 1) dipped from 884,5k to 758,0k. Following the rebirth of the Second Polish Republic (November 1918AD) and the 1919-1920AD Polish-Soviet War - which climaxed in Tukhachevsky's August 1920AD drive to the gates of Warsaw and high typhus/dysentery mortality in mutual prisoner-of-war camps [@udovenko2023camps] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_udovenko_2023_pow_camps_polish_lithuanian_soviet_wars.pdf)) - the 30 September 1921AD First Polish Census recorded 12 320k across Regions 1-4 (Warsaw 936,7k, Lodz 452,0k, Lublin 94,4k) [@gus1921skorowidz]. Organised repatriation trains under Article VII of the 18 March 1921AD Treaty of Riga returned over 1,1M civilian refugees and former POWs from Soviet Russia between 1921AD and 1924AD, lifting Congress Poland above its pre-war level to 13 830k by 1926AD (Warsaw 1 028,9k, Lodz 561,6k) [@baron2004homelands].

## Baltic Baltic Governorates: Estland, Livland and Courland (Regions 5 - 7)

Nowhere in the Russian Empire was First World War evacuation and industrial dismantling deeper than in Courland (Region 7, 27 588 km2) and southern Livland (Region 6, 54 235 km2). When the German *Niemen Army* invaded Courland in spring-summer 1915AD, Tsarist military authorities and Latvian relief committees evacuated more than half the rural peasantry alongside Jewish communities, slashing Courland by -52,5% from 800k (1914AD) to 380k (1917AD; Libau/Liepaja 90,7k to 43,2k, Mitau/Jelgava 45,7k to 21,5k and Windau/Ventspils 28,8k to 12,4k) [@gusachenko2021latvia; @skujenieks1927latvia] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_gusacenko_kleinberga_2021_latvia_state_1918.pdf)). Between 1915AD and 1917AD, Imperial authorities evacuated 395 factories and roughly 300 000 skilled metal, rubber (*Provodnik*) and electrical workers with their families from Riga to Moscow, Petrograd, Kharkov and Ekaterinoslav; tens of thousands of displaced Latvian workers and farmhands formed the Latvian Riflemen (*Latviesu strelnieki*), who subsequently served as the Praetorian core of the early Red Army. Following the 1918-1920AD Estonian and Latvian Wars of Independence - encompassing Soviet Latvian rule under Peteris Stucka, Baltic German *Landeswehr* fighting at Wenden/Cesis (June 1919AD) and Pavel Bermondt-Avalov's autumn 1919AD assault on Riga and burning of Mitau - the June 1920AD Latvian Census recorded Riga at just 185 137 (-64,2% below its 517 522 pre-war peak) [@skujenieks1927latvia]. Under the Peace Treaties of Tartu (2 February 1920AD with Estonia) and Riga (11 August 1920AD with Latvia), roughly 220 000 Latvian and 38 000 Estonian optants and refugees returned from Soviet Russia; by the 1922AD Estonian Census and 1925AD Latvian Census, Estland (Region 5) stood at 480k (498k in 1926AD; Tallinn 122,4k after shedding its 1917AD naval-fortress garrison peak of 159,0k), Livland reached 1 330k (1926AD; Riga 337,7k in 1925AD and 339,0k in 1926AD, Tartu 50,3k in 1922AD) and Courland recovered partially to 615k (-23,1% below 1914AD) [@estonia1924rahvaloendus; @skujenieks1927latvia].

## Southern and Northern Finland: The 1918AD Civil War and Camp Mortality (Regions 8 - 9)

Spared direct Eastern Front combat during 1914-1917AD, Southern Finland (Region 8: Nyland, Abo-Bjorneborg, Tavastehus and Vyborg, 114 315 km2) and Interior and Northern Finland (Region 9: Vasa, Kuopio, Sankt-Michel and Uleaborg, 263 819 km2) grew from 3 240k (1914AD) to 3 320k (1917AD) on Russian fortification employment before plunging into the brief, intensely lethal Finnish Civil War (27 January - 15 May 1918AD) shortly after independence [@upton1980finnish; @tikka2014finnish]. Industrial Red Guards controlled the southern urban triangle (Helsingfors, Tammerfors/Tampere, Kotka and Viipuri), while General Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim's White Senate mobilised Ostrobothnian and Karelian yeomanry from its provisional capital at Vasa and headquarters at Sankt-Michel. Following the April 1918AD urban siege of Tammerfors, German Baltic Sea Division landings at Hanko and Helsingfors and the capture of Viipuri, the Finnish National Archives *War Victims in Finland (1914-1922AD)* database documents 36 640 verified war-related deaths (estimated total 37 000 - 38 500, over 1,1% of the national population in four months): ~9 600 combat deaths, ~1 650 victims of Red Terror, ~8 400 - 10 000 victims of summary White field executions, and ~12 500 - 13 500 Red prisoners out of ~80 000 internees who perished between June and September 1918AD from acute starvation, dysentery and Spanish influenza in overcrowded prison camps at Tammisaari (Ekenas), Hameenlinna (Tavastehus), Hennala (Lahti), Suomenlinna and Viipuri [@rantala2020warvictims; @myrskyla2023finnish] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_myrskyla_santavirta_2023_finnish_civil_war_1918_mortality.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_rantala_jokipii_2020_war_victims_finland_1914_1922.pdf)). An additional 10 000 - 12 000 Red Finns fled across the Karelian Isthmus into Petrograd and Soviet Karelia (where Edvard Gylling organised the 1920AD Karelian Labour Commune), while 1918-1919AD Spanish influenza claimed ~20 000 civilian lives across Finland, depressing the combined population to 3 250k in 1918AD (1 845k in Region 8, 1 405k in Region 9) before steady peacetime recovery carried Finland to 3 305k in 1920AD and 3 605k by 1926AD (Helsingfors 215,8k, Abo/Turku 61,8k, Tammerfors 52,4k, Viipuri 51,5k) [@svt1923finland].

## Lithuania and Belarus: Ober Ost, Wilno and the Riga Partition (Regions 10 - 13)

Across the four Northwestern Krai provinces (304 761 km2; Regions 10-13), 1915AD Tsarist scorched-earth evacuations and three years of German *Ober Ost* requisitions (1915-1918AD) cut Kovno Governorate (Region 10) by -28,3% (1 840k to 1 320k) and Vilna and Grodno Governorates (Region 11) by -26,9% (3 940k to 2 880k, sliding further to 2 760k in 1920AD during four-way Polish-Lithuanian-Bolshevik fighting; Brest-Litovsk dropped from 57,4k to 16,5k in 1917AD) [@balkelis2018war; @gatrell1999whole]. After General Lucjan Zeligowski's October 1920AD mutiny detached Vilna/Wilno (204,3k in 1914AD -> 128,5k in 1919AD -> 178,0k in 1926AD) into Central Lithuania and subsequently Poland (1922AD), Kaunas (Kovno) served as the provisional capital of interwar Lithuania, surging from an Ober Ost low of 42,0k (1917AD) to 92,4k in the September 1923AD Lithuanian Census (94,4k in 1926AD) as ~250 000 - 300 000 Lithuanian refugees returned from interior Russia [@balkelis2018war; @marcinkevicius2026lithuania; @lithuania1926gyventojai] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_marcinkevicius_2026_russians_in_lithuania_1918_1940.pdf)). In Belarus (Region 12: Minsk and Region 13: Vitebsk & Mogilev), 1919-1920AD Polish-Soviet fronts, Bulak-Balakhovich's Polesian raids and typhus reduced Minsk Governorate from 3 040k (1914AD) to 2 680k (1920AD) and Vitebsk-Mogilev from 4 020k to 3 610k (Dvinsk/Daugavpils plummeting from 112,8k to 31,5k by 1920AD when Vitebsk's three Latgalian uezds joined Latvia). The 18 March 1921AD Treaty of Riga partitioned Belarus along the Polesian-Neman corridor [@cichoracki2014polesia] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_cichoracki_2014_polesia_after_riga_1921.pdf)): western Minsk (Pinsk, Baranovichi, Nowogrodek) and Grodno-Vilna entered Poland, while Soviet eastern Minsk formed the Belorussian SSR, enlarged in March 1924AD and December 1926AD with Vitebsk, Mogilev and Gomel uezds (4 983k in the 1926AD census; Minsk 131,8k, Vitebsk 98,9k, Gomel 86,4k) [@osipov2023natsionalnoy; @kryuchek2018belarus] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_osipov_nikita_aleksandrovich_2023_sravnitelnyy_analiz_natsionalnoy_politiki_.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_kryuchek_petr_stepanovich_2018_migratsionnye_protsessy_s_territorii_belar.pdf)).

## Eastern Galicia, Bukovina-Subcarpathia and Bessarabia (Regions 14 - 16)

In former Austro-Hungarian Eastern Galicia (Region 14, 46 070 km2), repeated 1914-1917AD Russian-Austrian offensives cut population from 5 020k to 4 450k (1917AD), and Habsburg collapse immediately ignited the November 1918 - July 1919AD Polish-Ukrainian War between the West Ukrainian People's Republic (*ZUNR*) and the Polish Republic over Lviv/Lwow (marked by the three-day November 1918AD Lviv pogrom) and the Drohobych-Boryslav oil basin, followed in summer 1920AD by Semyon Budyonny's First Cavalry Army sweep (Region 14 troughing at 4 290k in 1920AD before recovering via the 1921AD Polish Census 4 390k to 4 860k in 1926AD) [@mick2016galicia; @struve2014galicia; @gus1921skorowidz] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_mick_2016_war_lwow_eastern_galicia_1918_1920.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_struve_2014_eastern_galicia_peasants_1918_1921.pdf)). Across Region 15 (24 487 km2; 1 630k in 1914AD -> 1 450k in 1920AD -> 1 630k in 1926AD), Bukovina (Czernowitz 102,8k in 1926AD) united with Romania in November 1918AD, while Subcarpathian Rus (Uzhhorod, Mukachevo) joined Czechoslovakia under the 1919AD Treaty of Saint-Germain and 1920AD Treaty of Trianon (604,6k in the February 1921AD Czechoslovak Census) [@csr1924scitani]. In Bessarabia Governorate (Region 16, 47 379 km2), Romanian military intervention (January 1918AD) and the *Sfatul Tarii* union vote (27 March / 9 April 1918AD) severed the province from Odessa and the Dniester grain trade, sealing river bridges while triggering cross-Dniester refugee flight and three major anti-Romanian peasant and Bolshevik-backed insurrections - the Khotyn Uprising (January 1919AD) (sending ~50 000 refugees fleeing across the Dniester into Podolia), the Bender Uprising (May 1919AD) and the Tatarbunary Uprising (September 1924AD) in southern Budjak - depressing Bessarabia from 2 660k (1914AD) to 2 520k (1920AD) before rural natural increase restored 2 770k by 1926AD (Kishinev declining from 128,7k pre-war to 115,0k in 1926AD), while Moscow established the rival Moldavian ASSR (October 1924AD, first capital Balta) on the Ukrainian left bank [@tartakovsky2009bessarabia; @bondarenko2019bessarabia; @fondos2024bessarabia; @king2000moldovans] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_tartakovsky_2009_bessarabia_jewish_crisis_1918_1926.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_bondarenko_2019_bessarabia_romania_1918_1924.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_fondos_2024_bessarabia_interwar_population.pdf)).

# Ukraine, Urban Hollowing, the 1921-1922AD Famine, Caucasus and Siberia (Regions 17 - 48)

## Ukraine, the 1919AD Pogroms, Wrangel's Evacuation and Southern Steppe Famine (Regions 17 - 24)

Ukraine (Regions 17-24, 541 852 km2; 32 230k in 1914AD and 32 010k in 1917AD) was the most contested battlefield of the Civil War: Kyiv (644,0k in 1917AD -> 366,4k in 1920AD) changed hands more than a dozen times among the Central Rada, Pavlo Skoropadsky's German-backed Hetmanate, Symon Petliura's UNR Directory, the Red Army, Anton Denikin's Volunteer Army and the May 1920AD Polish-Ukrainian expedition [@kulchytsky2015demohrafichni]. Across Right-Bank Ukraine (Region 17: Volhynia, Region 18: Podolia and Region 19: Kyiv), 1918-1920AD brought the worst wave of anti-Jewish violence prior to the Shoah: over 1 300 documented pogroms perpetrated by insurgent *atamans* (Grigoriev, Zeleny, Struk), UNR Directory units, Denikin's White regiments and retreating cavalry slaughtered 100 000 - 150 000 Jews - with single-week massacres at Proskurov (February 1919AD), Fastov (September 1919AD), Felshtin, Bila Tserkva, Uman, Cherkassy and Berdichev - and displaced over 500 000 survivors from ruined shtetls into larger cities or emigration [@abramson1999prayer; @budnitskii2012russian; @veidlinger2021midst].

Across the southern Ukrainian steppe (Region 22: Kherson, Region 23: Ekaterinoslav and Region 24: Taurida), Nestor Makhno's Revolutionary Insurgent Army centred on Huliaipole (Ekaterinoslav), Denikin's 1919AD Moscow offensive and Baron Pyotr Wrangel's 1920AD Northern Taurida campaign devastated rail junctions and coal pits (Yuzovka, Lugansk, Krivoy Rog, Aleksandrovsk). In mid-November 1920AD, after the Red Army stormed the Perekop Isthmus, Wrangel evacuated 145 693 soldiers and civilians on 126 vessels from Sevastopol, Yalta, Feodosiya, Evpatoriya and Kerch to Constantinople, immediately followed by Bela Kun and Rozaliya Zemlyachka's Red Terror in Crimea (50 000 - 60 000 executed) [@kolesnikov2025zarubezhe; @smele2015russian] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_aleksandr_antonovich_kolesnikov_2025_russkoe_zarubezhe_v_turtsii_pisatel_gayto_.pdf)). Severe 1921-1922AD drought together with continued Soviet grain shipments from southern Ukraine to northern Russia then triggered the Southern Ukrainian and Crimean Famine (1921-1923AD), killing 300 000 - 500 000 across Zaporizhzhia, Ekaterinoslav, Nikolaev, Odessa (630,0k in 1914AD down -55,2% to 282,0k in 1922AD) and 100 000 in Crimea (disproportionately striking Crimean Tatar mountain and coastal villages within the newly created October 1921AD Crimean ASSR), driving Taurida down -32,2% (2 080k to 1 410k), Ekaterinoslav down -21,5% (3 580k to 2 810k) and Kherson down -21,2% (3 780k to 2 980k) before NEP recovery carried Regions 17-24 back to 31 890k in 1926AD (Kharkov, first UkSSR capital 1919-1934AD, surging to 417,3k) [@kulchytsky2015demohrafichni; @rozovyk2014bezhentsy] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_rozovyk_o_d_2014_mery_gosudarstvennykh_organov_vlasti_i_obs.pdf)).

## Capital De-Urbanisation in Petrograd and Moscow and the Tambov Peasant War (Regions 25 - 31)

Figure \ref{fig:fig4-urban} illustrates the unprecedented War Communism urban hollowing documented by the August 1920AD census [@koenker1985urbanization; @tsu1920perepis]. Cut off from Ukrainian coal, Baku oil and Siberian grain, and stripped of capital Ministries after Lenin relocated the Soviet government to Moscow in March 1918AD, Petrograd (Region 25: Saint Petersburg Governorate) lost -70,2% of its municipal population in three years - plunging from 2 420,0k (1917AD) to 1 469,0k (June 1918AD), 900,0k (1919AD, amid Nikolai Yudenich's Northwestern Army advance to Pulkovo Heights) and 722,2k (August 1920AD), pulling Saint Petersburg Governorate down -50,0% (3 380k to 1 690k, compounded by the March 1921AD suppression of the Kronstadt naval garrison and transfer of Narva to Estonia). Moscow (Region 28) fell -49,1% from 2 017,2k (September 1917AD) to 1 027,3k (August 1920AD, governorate 3 820k to 2 590k), while textile Ivanovo-Voznesensk (Region 29) dropped -60,4% (146,0k to 57,8k) as workers fled to native villages with hand-carts (*meshochniki*) [@koenker1985urbanization; @sutyrina2015transformatsii] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_sutyrina_o_n_2015_sotsialno_demograficheskie_transformatsii_.pdf)). Once NEP legalised private grain trade (March 1921AD) and reopened light industry, Moscow vaulted past its pre-war peak to 1 542,9k (1923AD) and 2 025,9k (December 1926AD, governorate 4 180k), while Leningrad recovered to 1 071,1k (1923AD) and 1 614,0k (1926AD, governorate 2 690k) [@tsu1923gorod; @tsu1926vsesoyuznaya].

```{r fig4-urban, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
render_figure_template(
  "figures/russian_civil_war_fig4_urban_hierarchy.png",
  list(
    caption = "Population trajectories of the 22 largest cities across the pre-war Tsarist regions at the 1914AD, 1920AD, and 1926AD benchmarks in thousands.",
    label = "fig:fig4-urban",
    span_columns = TRUE
  )
)
```

In the European North (Region 27: 2 280k to 2 130k to 2 390k), British-American-French intervention forces occupied Murmansk (Romanov-on-Murman) and Arkhangelsk (1918-1920AD), followed in August 1921AD by creation of the Komi (Zyryan) AO (Ust-Sysolsk). Across the Central Black-Earth Belt (Regions 30-31), Denikin's autumn 1919AD advance reached Kursk and Oryol (Region 30: 8 180k to 7 360k), while ruthless *prodrazvyorstka* grain requisitions in Tambov and Voronezh (Region 31: 9 450k in 1917AD down to 8 340k in 1922AD, -11,7%) ignited Aleksandr Antonov's 40 000-strong Antonovshchina peasant war (August 1920 - summer 1921AD), suppressed by Mikhail Tukhachevsky with 100 000 Red troops, hostage concentration camps, village deportations and chemical shells [@dyachkov2021tambov; @esikova2017tambov; @safonov2020nep] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_dyachkov_vladimir_lvovich_2021_revolyutsiya_1917_goda_i_grazhdanskaya_voy.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_esikova_milana_mikhaylovna_2017_razrabotka_problem_krestyanskogo_dvizheniy.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_safonov_dmitriy_anatolevich_2020_nep_i_krestyanskiy_protest_1921_1922_gg_iz.pdf)).

## The 1921-1922AD Povolzhye-Ural Famine, Pandemics and ARA Relief (Regions 32 - 34, 39 - 40)

The single deadliest demographic catastrophe of the epoch struck the Volga-Kama-Ural basin (Regions 32-34 and 39-40, 1 442 819 km2) in 1921-1922AD. Three consecutive years of *prodrazvyorstka* requisitions stripped peasant seed reserves across Samara, Saratov, Simbirsk, Kazan and Ufa just before an extreme spring-summer 1921AD anticyclonic drought burned out 60-85% of the harvest, coinciding with 25M-30M Soviet-wide cases of louse-borne epidemic typhus and relapsing fever (2,5M-3,0M deaths across 1918-1922AD), 1921AD Volga cholera and 1918-1919AD Spanish influenza (~1,5M-2,0M deaths) [@tarasevich1922epidemics; @wheatcroft1981famine; @prokhorov1999krizisy; @morozova2021ispanka; @timofeeva2006demograficheskie] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_prokhorov_b_b_1999_krizisy_obshchestvennogo_zdorovya_v_rossii.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_morozova_o_m_2021_pandemiya_ispanki_1918_goda_v_rossii_vopro.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_timofeeva_tatyana_fedorovna_2006_demograficheskie_problemy_kasayushchiesya_.pdf)):

Samara and Saratov Governorates (Region 33, incl. the Volga German Labour Commune / ASSR) contracted by -27,2% (7 120k in 1917AD to 6 580k in 1920AD to 5 180k in 1922AD, -1 940k), with rural Pugachyov and Buzuluk uezds and the Volga German colonies (Pokrovsk/Engels, Marxstadt, established as an autonomous commune in October 1918AD and ASSR in January 1924AD) suffering 25-35% population loss through starvation and chaotic flight before partial recovery to 6 020k in 1926AD [@polyakov2005povolzhskiy; @badmaeva2010golod] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_v_l_polyakov_2005_povolzhskiy_golod_nachala_1920_kh_gg_k_ist.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_badmaeva_ekaterina_nikolaevna_2010_golod_v_nizhnem_povolzhe_v_1921_i_1933_gg.pdf)).

Ufa and Orenburg Governorates (Region 40, incl. the Bashkir ASSR) plunged by -27,7% (5 480k in 1917AD to 3 960k in 1922AD, -1 520k; 4 660k in 1926AD). Created in March 1919AD as the first Soviet autonomous republic (*Little Bashkiria*, expanded with Ufa Governorate into *Greater Bashkiria* in June 1922AD), rural Bashkir cantons experienced catastrophic famine and typhus losses exceeding 25-30%, compounded by Ataman Aleksandr Dutov's 1918-1919AD Orenburg Cossack campaigns and the transfer of southern Orenburg steppe districts to the Kirghiz (Kazakh) ASSR [@mints2022golod; @martin2001affirmative; @feldman2001ural; @zhuravleva2013khozyaeva] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_mints_mikhail_mikhaylovich_2022_golod_v_sssr_1930_1933_gg.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_feldman_mikhail_arkadevich_2001_chislennost_sostav_sotsialnyy_oblik_raboch.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_zhuravleva_vera_anatolevna_2013_sotsialnaya_gruppa_khozyaeva_sredi_gorozha.pdf)).

Middle Volga (Region 32), Lower Volga-Astrakhan (Region 34) and Northern Urals (Region 39): Region 32 (Nizhny Novgorod, Kazan, Simbirsk and Penza, encompassing the May 1920AD Tatar ASSR and June 1920AD Chuvash AO) declined -20,7% (8 550k to 6 780k, severe mortality in Tatar and Chuvash villages); Region 34 (Astrakhan and the November 1920AD Kalmyk AO) fell -25,5% (1 410k to 1 050k) [@badmaeva2010golod; @badmaeva2020istoriografiya] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_badmaeva_ekaterina_nikolaevna_2020_demograficheskaya_istoriya_sssr_v_1920_193.pdf)); and Region 39 (Perm and Vyatka, including the November 1920AD Votsk/Udmurt and Mari AOs and Kolchak's 1919AD Perm offensive) fell -15,9% (8 040k to 6 760k).


Following Maxim Gorky's July 1921AD international appeal and the August 1921AD Riga Agreement, Herbert Hoover's American Relief Administration (ARA), Fridtjof Nansen's International Committee, the American Friends Service Committee and Pomgol established soup kitchens and medical stations from Kazan to Orenburg and Odessa, feeding over 10,5M Soviet citizens daily at peak operation in August 1922AD and preventing several million additional deaths [@patenaude2002big]. Table \ref{tab:loss-synthesis} synthesises demographic reconstructions of 1918-1922AD excess mortality across Soviet and post-Soviet scholarship (~5,0M excess deaths in the 1921-1922AD famine within 8,0M-10,5M total 1918-1922AD excess military, terror, epidemic and famine deaths, plus 1,5M-2,0M White/civilian emigrants) [@volkov1930dinamika; @lorimer1946population; @wheatcroft1981famine; @polyakov1986sovetskaya; @maksudov1989poteri; @andreev1993naselenie].

```{r table-loss-synthesis, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
loss_df <- data.frame(
  `Demographic Study / Reconstruction` = c(
    "Volkov (1930) - TsSU Dynamic Reconstruction",
    "Lorimer (1946) - League of Nations USSR Balance",
    "Wheatcroft (1981) - Mortality & 1921-22 Famine",
    "Polyakov (1986) & Zhiromskaya-Polyakov (2000)",
    "Maksudov (1989) - Demographic Losses of USSR",
    "Andreev, Darsky & Kharkova (1993) - Goskomstat",
    "Present 48-Region Tsarist Synthesis (1914-1926AD)"
  ),
  `Spatial Domain` = c(
    "USSR Interwar Borders",
    "USSR 1926AD Territory",
    "USSR Famine & Epidemic Zones",
    "Soviet Territory (1917-1922AD)",
    "USSR Territory (1918-1922AD)",
    "RSFSR & USSR Back-Projection",
    "48 Pre-War Tsarist Regions"
  ),
  `1918-22 Excess Deaths` = c(
    "~7,0M - 8,5M",
    "~9,0M - 10,0M (incl. deficit)",
    "~5,0M (1921-22 Famine/Typhus)",
    "~8,0M - 10,0M (+2,0M emigr.)",
    "~7,8M - 9,5M (+2,0M emigr.)",
    "~8,5M - 10,5M (1921-22: ~5,0M)",
    "~9,5M - 10,8M (+Finn./Border)"
  ),
  `Key Finding` = c(
    "Documents 1920AD urban collapse & ~5,0M 1921-22 famine toll",
    "14M+ total deficit incl. birth losses & ~2,0M out-migration",
    "Isolates louse-borne typhus & Povolzhye-Ural harvest failure",
    "Integrates Civil War fronts, Red/White Terror & emigration",
    "Separates combat/terror (~2,5M), typhus (~3M) & famine (~4-5M)",
    "Age-sex cohort back-projection from 1926AD All-Union Census",
    "167 945k (1914) -> 148 655k (1922) -> 167 780k (1926)"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

render_table_template(
  loss_df,
  list(
    caption = "Comparative Demographic Estimates of Excess Mortality, Famine Losses and Emigration (1918AD - 1922AD).",
    label = "tab:loss-synthesis",
    col_fracs = c(0.25, 0.19, 0.19, 0.27)
  )
)
```

## Decossackisation, Caucasian Highland Wars and Early Autonomies (Regions 35 - 38)

Across the Cossack and North Caucasian belt (Regions 35-38, 434 845 km2), Civil War fronts overlapped with systematic Bolshevik decossackisation (*raskazachivanie*) and highland ethno-territorial restructuring [@holquist2002making; @venkov2018kazachestvo; @matsievskiy2011kazachestvo] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_venkov_andrey_vadimovich_2018_genotsid_golodomor_i_drugie_uzhasy_v_istor.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_matsievskiy_german_olegovich_2011_osnovnye_etapy_politicheskoy_istorii_rossi.pdf)):

Don Cossack Host (Region 35, -21,6%, 3 940k to 3 090k) and Kuban-Black Sea (Region 36, -20,2%, 3 120k to 2 490k): Following Kaledin and Krasnov's Don campaigns, the Orgburo's 24 January 1919AD circular ordering mass terror against upper-Don Cossack elites triggered the March-June 1919AD Veshenskaya Uprising, followed by the catastrophic winter 1919-1920AD Don-Kuban retreat, the chaotic March 1920AD White evacuation from Novorossiysk, Cossack deportations and the 1921-1922AD Salsk-Kuban drought (Adygei [Cherkess] AO formed July 1922AD).

Stavropol and Terek Oblast (Region 37, -16,2%, 2 650k to 2 220k) and Dagestan Oblast (Region 38, -14,5%, 725k to 620k): Fierce 1918-1920AD fighting pitted Terek Cossack *stanitsas* against Chechen and Ingush highlanders (August-November 1918AD Hundred Days Battle of Grozny). In spring-autumn 1920AD, Sergo Ordzhonikidze ordered the forced expulsion and deportation of 45 000 - 70 000 Terek Cossacks from Assinovskaya, Sernovodskaya, Ermolovskaya, Zakan-Yurtovskaya and Kalinovskaya *stanitsas* along the Sunzha line, transferring their lands to Vainakh highlanders and establishing the Mountain ASSR (20 January 1921AD, capital Vladikavkaz), which subsequently devolved (1921-1924AD) into the Kabardino-Balkar, Karachay-Cherkess, Chechen, North Ossetian and Ingush autonomous oblasts while Grozny boomed on NEP oil reconstruction (2k in 1914AD to 97,1k in 1926AD) [@martin2001affirmative]. Simultaneously in Dagestan (Dagestan ASSR proclaimed 20 January 1921AD, capital shifted from Temir-Khan-Shura/Buynaksk to Petrovsk-Port/Makhachkala), Imam Najmuddin Gotsinsky and Kailasan Alikhanov led the bloody September 1920 - May 1921AD Avar-Andi mountain uprising across Gunib and Khunzakh before Red 11th Army suppression.


## Siberia, the Great Siberian Ice March and the Far Eastern Republic (Regions 41 - 48)

Across Siberia and the Far East (Regions 41-48, 12 854 849 km2), population held near or above pre-war levels (12 470k in 1914AD -> 12 875k in 1917AD -> 12 665k in 1920AD -> 12 730k in 1922AD -> 14 652k in 1926AD) because inward peasant flight from the starving Volga-Ural provinces offset severe localized military and epidemic mortality [@smele2015russian; @polyakov1986sovetskaya]:

Kolchak's Omsk, the 1919-1920AD Great Siberian Ice March and the 1921AD West Siberian Revolt (Regions 41-45): Following the May 1918AD Czechoslovak Legion revolt along the Trans-Siberian trunk, Admiral Aleksandr Kolchak established his White Supreme Ruler government in Omsk (Region 41), swelling the city with ministries, officers and refugees from 148,0k (1917AD) to ~245,0k (summer 1919AD). When Tukhachevsky's 5th Red Army took Omsk in November 1919AD, General Vladimir Kappel led the winter 1919-1920AD Great Siberian Ice March (*Velikiy Sibirskiy Ledyanoy Pokhod*) 2 000 km eastward through -40C frosts across Novonikolaevsk (Region 43), Taiga, Achinsk, Krasnoyarsk, Kansk and frozen Lake Baikal to Irkutsk (Region 45, where Kolchak was executed in February 1920AD); raging railway-car typhus killed tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians at Novonikolaevsk (0k in 1919AD down to 67,2k in August 1920AD before leaping to 120,1k by 1926AD as Siberian krai capital) and Krasnoyarsk (0k to 60,8k) [@smele2015russian]. In February-June 1921AD, punitive grain requisitions in Ishim, Tobolsk, Kurgan and Tyumen provoked the 60 000-strong West Siberian Peasant Uprising, severing both Trans-Siberian rail lines for three weeks [@borodin2012siberia; @burdina2017siberia] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_borodin_dmitriy_yurevich_2012_zapadnosibirskoe_vosstanie_1921_g_v_angloy.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_burdina_elena_nikolaevna_2017_obshchestvenno_politicheskie_nastroeniya_k.pdf)). Meanwhile, Altai partisan strongholds (Barnaul, Biysk in Region 43) absorbed hundreds of thousands of famine migrants, while in Region 44 (Altai-Sayan & Uriankhai) Moscow sponsored the August 1921AD Tannu-Tuva People's Republic (Kyzyl/Belotsarsk) alongside the June 1922AD Oyrot (Gorny Altai) AO and Khakass Okrug.

The Far Eastern Republic, Yakut Revolt and Japanese Evacuation (Regions 46-48): East of Lake Baikal (Regions 47-48), Lenin authorised the Far Eastern Republic (FER, 6 April 1920 - 15 November 1922AD, capital Chita from October 1920AD) as a democratic buffer state to avoid direct war with 70 000 Japanese Intervention troops while liquidating Ataman Grigory Semyonov in Transbaikalia and Baron Roman von Ungern-Sternberg along the Kyakhta-Mongolian frontier (Buryat-Mongol ASSR established May 1923AD) [@tumurkhonova2009buryat] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_tumurkhonova_nina_vasilevna_2009_selskokhozyaystvennye_perepisi_v_buryat_mo.pdf)). In Yakutia (Region 47, Yakut ASSR proclaimed 27 April 1922AD), the 1921-1923AD Yakut Revolt and White General Anatoly Pepelyaev's 1922-1923AD Okhotsk-Ayan-Amga expedition ended the last armed White campaign in Russia just before the 1924AD Aldan gold rush. In Priamurye and Sakhalin (Region 48), partisan commander Yakov Tryapitsyn burned Nikolaevsk-on-Amur in May 1920AD (4k down to 3,2k), provoking Japanese occupation of Northern Sakhalin (1920-1925AD, returned under the January 1925AD Beijing Convention). Following the October 1922AD Spassk offensive, Japanese forces evacuated Vladivostok on 25 October 1922AD alongside Admiral Georgy Stark's 30-ship White flotilla (~10 000 evacuees to Wonsan and Shanghai) and tens of thousands of White emigres crossing into Harbin, Manchuria, after which the FER merged into the RSFSR (Vladivostok stabilising from 136,0k refugee peak in 1921AD to 108,0k in 1926AD) [@chzhan2017emigratsiya; @temirgaleev2017primorye] ([archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_chzhan_tszunkhua_2017_russkaya_dvoryanskaya_emigratsiya_v_kitae_.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/russian_civil_war_temirgaleev_renat_faritovich_2017_ukraintsy_primorskogo_kraya_v_1897_2010_gg.pdf)).


# Spatial Methodology, Cross-Epoch Continuity and Validation

Pixel-Exact Continuity with Pre-War Imperial Russia: russian_civil_war_areal_mask.png (48 regions, 460 079 pixels, 18 607 231 km2) preserves the exact pre-war Tsarist Governorate and Oblast polygons of imperial_russia_post_1815, guaranteeing zero boundary discontinuity across the 1914AD (167 945k) and 1917AD (165 375k) splice years while explicitly accounting for all 1918-1926AD secession and internal boundary realignments in Table \ref{tab:splice-1926}. Complete 48-Region Settlement Gazetteer (275 settlements) covers 100% of all forty-eight region IDs (4-8 cities per region) across all nine benchmark years [1914, 1917, 1918, 1919, 1920, 1921, 1922, 1924, 1926].
